connection_type: I'm a caregiver, partner, or close community member of someone with this experience
disclosure_text: I work within the juvenile justice field and some of my kids are not documented or their parents are afraid to go to court in fears of being deported.
micronarrative:
I love the idea that the community banded together to support the bakery. It is disgusting to think that because the business holds certain religious beliefs, their business should be boycotted. Being told that they are erasing the traditional culture of the town is frightening and shows that there are some people within it that are closeminded and dangerous. I've witnessed many injustices and closemindedness firsthand. When ICE came into our local community, some kids made jokes about people being deported back to their countries. There were some kids whose parents were undocumented who didn't want to speak up against the organization. There were other kids and staff who explained how harmful ICE can be, especially with removals where detainees couldn't contact their lawyers or family members.

My economic situation doesn't really affect my opinions on these matters. It's more related to the fact that my grandparents immigrated to the United States from Mexico. My mom shared a story of how when she was growing up, the neighbors would call immigration on my grandparents and her siblings. By that point, they had proper documentation, but it was still very frightening to have ICE agents coming to the home at all times of the day and night. 

Now is the greatest time to show our support for local communities and band together to protect one another. We need to stand up for those who are vulnerable and ensure that everyone feels safe and valued in our community.
